note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 6(3), BHU 4; A06b Const 6(3), BHU 4; L05 Const 6(5), BHU 6(a)): ordinary naturalisation after 20 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Dual citizenship restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Dual citizenship restriction), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a dual-citizenship restriction on descent, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primaries were read: The Bhutan Citizen Act, 1985 (Depository of Laws, Office of the Attorney General, legislation.gov.bt, legislation id 143, enacted 1985-06-10), sections as served by the depository's own API; The Constitution of the Kingdom of Bhutan, 2008, Article 6 (Citizenship) (Depository of Laws, legislation id 79), as served by the depository's own API. They confirmed the years of residence, renunciation, loss on taking another citizenship, birth in the territory and the limit abroad. The Constitution (art. 6(1)) and the Act (s. 2) make a child a citizen at birth only when both parents are citizens; the form has no value for both parents, so the nearest, either parent, is kept (it errs for a child with one Bhutanese parent, whom the game makes Bhutanese), and the entry isn't wholly found on that figure. The Act's 20 years are for an applicant who is neither a government employee nor a citizen's child (15 for those); the Constitution's floor is fifteen.

sources.title: The Bhutan Citizen Act, 1985 (Depository of Laws, Office of the Attorney General, legislation.gov.bt, legislation id 143, enacted 1985-06-10), sections as served by the depository's own API
sources.said: 2. CITIZENSHIP BY BIRTH. A person whose parents are both citizens of Bhutan shall be deemed to be a citizen of Bhutan by birth. ... 4. CITIZENSHIP BY NATURALIZATION ... c) The person must have resided in Bhutan for 15 years in the case of Government employees and also in the case of applicants, either of whose parents is a citizen of Bhutan, and 20 years in all other case, and this period of residence must be registered in the records of the Department of Immigration and Census. ... 6. TERMINATION OF CITIZENSHIP: a) Any citizen of Bhutan who acquires the citizenship of another country shall cease to be a citizen of Bhutan.

sources.title: The Constitution of the Kingdom of Bhutan, 2008, Article 6 (Citizenship) (Depository of Laws, legislation id 79), as served by the depository's own API
sources.said: 1. A person, both of whose parents are citizens of Bhutan, shall be a natural born citizen of Bhutan. ... 3. A person who applies for citizenship by naturalization shall: (a) Have lawfully resided in Bhutan for at least fifteen years; ... (f) Renounce the citizenship, if any, of a foreign State on being conferred Bhutanese citizenship; ... 5. If any citizen of Bhutan acquires the citizenship of a foreign State, his or her citizenship of Bhutan shall be terminated.

atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born abroad to two citizens.
